blocks.text: - Know the importance of the topographical division of the mediastinum.
- Know the limits of the mediastinum.
- Know the limits of each compartment.
- Know the contents of each compartment.

rows: - Know how to locate the mediastinum.

blocks.text: III-Topographic anatomy: -International division proposed by Nomina Anatomica (anatomo-surgical division).

1- Superior mediastinum: Limits: ? In front: manubrium of the sternum. ? Posteriorly: anterior edge of TH4. ? At the top: the upper opening of the thorax. ? Bottom: transverse line crossing the carina and the aortic arch. Content: ? Upper third of the esophagus. ? Large vessels and their branches. ? Trachea. ? Superior vena cava. ? Upper pole of the thymus. ? Phrenic, pneumogastric, cardiac and recurrent left laryngeal nerves. ? Arterial ligament. ? Thoracic duct. ? Upper paratracheal and tracheobronchial lymph nodes.
2- Anterior mediastinum: Limits: ? In front: sternum. ? Behind: anterior surface of the pericardium. Content: ? Internal thoracic vessels. ? Parasternal and pre-pericardial lymph nodes.

3- Middle mediastinum: Limits: ? In front: anterior surface of the pericardium. ? Behind: posterior surface of the pericardium. Content: ? Heart in its pericardial sac. ? Pulmonary vessels. ? Phrenic nerves. ? Lateropericardial and lower tracheobronchial lymph nodes. 4- Posterior mediastinum: Limits: ? In front: posterior surface of the pericardium. ? Behind: anterior surface of the dorsal spine. Content: ? The thoracic esophagus. ? The thoracic aorta. ?The thoracic duct. ? Azygos and hemi-azygos veins. ? Pneumogastric and splanchnic nerves. ? Juxta-esophageal, prevertebral and upper phrenic pulmonary nodes.
